summary: Cab on an AT&T electronics building roof on Cedro Peak in the Sandia Ranger District since 1969; earlier towers date to the 1920s and 1935. Blog reports it locked and not staffed.

facts.design: 14x14 ft metal CL-100 series cab placed on the roof of an AT&T electronics building beside a transmission tower

staffing.status: not staffed; fires watched mostly by satellite (personal blog)

access.note: Access road reported gated and the lookout locked, per a personal blog (undated); no Forest Service notice was found.

visit.trail_note: The blog reports visitors may not use the stairway to the balcony.

events.note: A wood fire lookout tower with a roofless platform was on the peak by 1922
Department of Commerce permit for a 40-ft steel beacon tower; the Forest Service was to use it as a lookout
CCC crew built a new steel tower (register: 45-ft metal tower), cabin and road; replaced the older tower
Summer lookout staffed by a chief lookout and an assistant
Fire guards entered on duty at the lookout for the fire season
AT&T built a transmission tower and a replacement building; the present 14x14 ft cab was placed on the building roof
1988 National Register thematic evaluation found the lookout not eligible due to age

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 'Built' field gives 1969, which matches the present cab on the AT&T building. Lookouts on the peak date to the 1920s and the 1935 CCC tower, so 1969 is not the first build.
The register gives a 25-ft log tower; the 1935 newspaper calls the old tower a 30-foot pole tower. The story gives both.
The register gives a 45-ft metal tower. The 1935 article says the frame rose more than 45 feet above the summit. A 1945 article describes a 50-foot tower.

notes_for_editor: Height: the record's height_m 9.1 (30 ft) has no source for the current structure; 30 ft matches the old pole tower the 1935 article describes, so it is probably wrong. Remove or re-measure; no correction entry was made because no replacement value is supported. Built: record's 1969 is the present cab, not the first lookout. Access and staffing rest on one undated personal blog; no Forest Service notice was read. The blog includes a route to the lookout, which is deliberately not used here; do not add it. The 2020 report says the 1988 evaluation mistyped the cab as an MC-39 (a 7x7 ft cab). Fire, staffing and access for 2026 are unverified. No photos added. Fact check 2026-10-08: the register page has no 'standing' status, so that sentence was removed from the story.
